messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (hosted-us-west-2). SLO p99 > 4s for the last 5m — autopage triggered to on-call. Pager: pd-ops -> page fired.
juan: Acked. I'm on it. Looking at traces and the inference-frontend dashboards now.
juan: Dashboard shows p50 ~120ms p95 ~420ms p99 ~5.8s. Error rate unchanged. High tail on tokenization stage per trace waterfall.
maya: Any recent rollouts to tokenizer-service or model variants?
juan: There was a canary of tokenizer v2 at 09:10 UTC (small rollout). Canary traffic is ~3% but I see warmup thrash on pooled workers.
danielle: Might be autoscaler churn on tokenizer pods — scale up then OOM/evict then scale back. Check HPA events and node preemptions.
juan: Pulling HPA events...
juan: ```
kubectl -n infra get hpa tokenizer -o yaml
# HPA minReplicas:1 maxReplicas:30 targetCPU:60
# LastScale: scaled from 3 -> 18 at 1761234400
```
juan: Node events show several pod evictions on us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 in the last 8m due to ephemeral disk pressure.
juan: That matches the pattern: tokenizer cold-starts + KV cache misses + autoscaler overshoot = tail latency heatwave.
claire: Customer impact — charts show 12% of requests in the chat flow hit p99. Top affected tenants: org-omega (EU) and org-kite (US-West). No visible 5xx increase but UX latency spike reported by support.
tom: Quick mitigations we can do: 1) route a fraction of traffic to fallback tokenizer (v1, smaller mem) 2) bump HPA minReplicas to 6 temporarily 3) cordon/evacuate noisy node and trigger node replace 4) enable model fallthrough to small-model for non-critical routes.
juan: I'll flip a routing rule to divert 20% to tokenizer-v1 and scale tokenizer HPA minReplicas to 6 now. Applying runbook step 2 and 4.
juan: ```
# route config change (feature flag)
redwoodctl route set tokenizer-fallback --selector=chat --percent=20
kubectl -n infra patch hpa/tokenizer --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
```
incident-bot: NOTE: runbook step initiated by juan: tokenizer fallback route set, HPA patched.
maya: Good. Also can we temporarily disable the new tokenizer canary? If it's only 3% it might still be causing cache churn.
juan: Disabling canary now. ```redwoodctl rollout cancel tokenizer:v2 --canary```
juan: After routing change + bumping minReplicas, p99 dropped from 5.8s -> 2.1s in ~90s. p95 stable ~400ms.
danielle: Nice. We should also warm the KV cache for tokenizer to reduce cold misses — running a small synthetic warmup job for hot prefixes.
claire: I'll notify support and prepare a brief customer note: impacted tenants, mitigation applied, ETA on full stabilization ~15m.
juan: Leaving a note in postmortem tracker: suspected cause = node disk pressure + tokenizer canary warm-up causing autoscaler thrash -> increased cold starts -> p99 tail. Action items: (1) revert tokenizer canary until stability playbook done, (2) add HPA safety buffer for tokenizer, (3) add node disk pressure alert to infra.
maya: Handing over to me for the next shift. I'll watch for reoccurrence and follow up with infra to replace the noisy node.
juan: Thanks — I'll add runbook anchors and the exact commands to the incident doc. Tagging SRE manager for awareness. @danielle mind escalating to PD manager if p99 resurges?
danielle: Yep — will escalate if we see >2 recurrences in 1h.
pagerduty-bot: Pager duty note: incident acknowledged by juan at 1761234570. No escalation fired.
claire: Support update sent to affected customers, link pasted to thread.
maya: Monitoring: p99 holding ~2.0s, continuing to trend down. I'll keep the HPA minReplicas and fallback route for 30m then reevaluate.
juan: Closing initial triage, leaving follow-ups in the incident board. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
